103624.subject: Physics
103624.text:
A small circular loop of area $A$ and resistance $R$ is fixed on a horizontal $xy$-plane with the center of the loop always on the axis $\overset{^}{n}$ of a long solenoid. The solenoid has $m$ turns per unit length and carries current $I$ counter clockwise as shown in the figure. The magnetic field due to the solenoid is in $\overset{^}{n}$ direction. List-I gives time dependences of $\overset{^}{n}$ in terms of a constant angular frequency $\omega$. List-II gives the torques experienced by the circular loop at time $t = \dfrac{\pi}{6\omega}$, Let $\alpha = \dfrac{{A}^{2}{\mu}_{0}^{2}{m}^{2}{I}^{2}\omega}{2R}$.

  List-I   List-II
(i) $\dfrac{1}{\sqrt{2}}\left(sin\omegat\overset{^}{j} + cos\omegat\overset{^}{k}\right)$ (p) $0$
(ii) $\dfrac{1}{\sqrt{2}}\left(sin\omegat\overset{^}{i} + cos\omegat\overset{^}{j}\right)$ (q) $- \dfrac{\alpha}{4}\overset{^}{i}$
(iii) $\dfrac{1}{\sqrt{2}}\left(sin\omegat\overset{^}{i} + cos\omegat\overset{^}{k}\right)$ (r) $\dfrac{3\alpha}{4}\overset{^}{i}$
(iv) $\dfrac{1}{\sqrt{2}}\left(cos\omegat\overset{^}{j} + sin\omegat\overset{^}{k}\right)$ (s) $\dfrac{\alpha}{4}\overset{^}{j}$
    (t) $- \dfrac{3\alpha}{4}\overset{^}{i}$

Which one of the following options is correct?
options: $i \to q, ii \to p, iii \to s, iv \to t$
$i \to s, ii \to t, iii \to q, iv \to p$
$i \to q, ii \to p, iii \to s, iv \to r$
$i \to t, ii \to q, iii \to p, iv \to r$
103624.sol:
Note: This question was given bonus by JEE council.

The magnetic field in a solenoid is given by, $\overset{\to}{B} = {\mu}_{0}mI\overset{^}{n}$. Therefore, the flux through the loop will be,

$ϕ = \left(A\overset{^}{k}\right) \cdot \left({\mu}_{0}mI\overset{^}{n}\right)$

For case I:

$ϕ = \dfrac{BA}{\sqrt{2}}cos\left(\omegat\right)$

The emf will be,

$ε = \dfrac{BA\omega}{\sqrt{2}}sin\left(\omegat\right)$

Therefore, the current in the loop will be,

$i = \dfrac{BA\omega}{\sqrt{2}R}sin\left(\omegat\right)$

The magnetic moment of the loop will be,

$\overset{\to}{m} = iA\overset{^}{k} = \dfrac{B{A}^{2}\omega}{\sqrt{2}R}sin\left(\omegat\right)\overset{^}{k}$

Therefore, the torque

$\overset{\to}{τ} = \overset{\to}{m} \times \overset{\to}{B} = \dfrac{{B}^{2}{A}^{2}\omega}{\sqrt{2}R}sin\left(\omegat\right)\left(\overset{^}{k} \times \overset{^}{n}\right)$

$⇒ \overset{\to}{τ} = - \dfrac{{B}^{2}{A}^{2}\omega}{2R}\left[\overset{^}{i}\right]\sin^{2}\left(\omegat\right)$

$⇒ \overset{\to}{τ} = - \dfrac{{B}^{2}{A}^{2}\omega}{2R}\left[\sin^{2}\left(\dfrac{\pi}{6}\right)\right] = \dfrac{- \alpha}{4}\overset{^}{i}$

Hence, $\left(I\right) \to q$

For case II

$ϕ = 0$

Therefore, we can directly write $τ = 0$

Hence $\left(II\right) \to p$

Following the same process as in case I for case III

$ϕ = \dfrac{BA}{\sqrt{2}}cos\left(\omegat\right)$

$i = \dfrac{BA\omega}{\sqrt{2}R}sin\left(\omegat\right)$

$\overset{\to}{m} = \dfrac{B{A}^{2}\omega}{\sqrt{2}R}sin\left(\omegat\right)\overset{^}{k}$

$\overset{\to}{τ} = \overset{\to}{m} \times \overset{\to}{B} = \dfrac{{B}^{2}{A}^{2}\omega}{\sqrt{2} \times \sqrt{2}R}sin\omegat\left(\overset{^}{k} \times \left(sin\omegat\overset{^}{i} + cos\omegat\overset{^}{k}\right)\right)$

$\overset{\to}{τ} = \dfrac{{B}^{2}{A}^{2}\omegasin\left(\omegat\right)}{2R}sin\left(\omegat\right)\overset{^}{j}$

$\overset{\to}{τ} = \dfrac{{B}^{2}{A}^{2}\omega}{2R}\sin^{2}\left(\omegat\right)\overset{^}{j}$

$\overset{\to}{τ} = \dfrac{\alpha}{4}\overset{^}{j}$

Hence, $III \to s$

Following the same process as in case I for case IV

$ϕ = \dfrac{BA}{\sqrt{2}}sin\left(\omegat\right)$

$i = - \dfrac{BA\omega}{\sqrt{2}R}cos\left(\omegat\right)$

$\overset{\to}{m} = - \dfrac{B{A}^{2}\omega}{\sqrt{2}R}cos\omegat\left(\overset{^}{k}\right)$

$\overset{\to}{τ} = \overset{\to}{m} \times \overset{\to}{B} = - \dfrac{{B}^{2}{A}^{2}\omega}{2R}\left(\overset{^}{k} \times \overset{^}{j}\right)\cos^{2}\left(\omegat\right)$

$\overset{\to}{τ} = + \dfrac{{B}^{2}{A}^{2}\omega}{2R}\left(\overset{^}{i}\right) \cdot \cos^{2}\left(\dfrac{\pi}{6}\right)$

$\overset{\to}{τ} = + \dfrac{3}{4}\alpha\overset{^}{i}$

Hence, $\left(IV\right) \to r$

103704.subject: Physics
103704.text: A very long conducting wire carrying a steady current $i$ is bent into a hairpin shape consisting of two parallel semi-infinite straight segments and a semi-circular arc of radius $R$. The arc lies in the $xy$-plane, centered at the origin, and spans from $(0, R)$ to $(0, -R)$ through the region $x > 0$. The top straight segment lies along $y = R$ and the bottom straight segment lies along $y = -R$. The current $i$ flows from $x = +\infty$ to $x = 0$ along the top segment, follows the semi-circular arc, and then flows from $x = 0$ to $x = +\infty$ along the bottom segment. An electron is projected from the origin with speed $v$ in the $-x$ direction. What is the magnitude and initial direction of the magnetic force acting on the electron?
options: $\dfrac{\mu_0 e v i}{4 R} \left[1 - \dfrac{2}{\pi}\right]$ towards the bottom segment
$\dfrac{\mu_0 e v i}{4 R} \left[1 + \dfrac{2}{\pi}\right]$ towards the top segment
$\dfrac{\mu_0 e v i}{4 R} \left[1 - \dfrac{2}{\pi}\right]$ towards the top segment
103704.sol:
Step 1: Calculate the net magnetic field $\vec{B}$ at the origin.

The top semi-infinite segment carries current in the $-x$ direction. Using the right-hand rule, its magnetic field at the origin is directed out of the page ($+z$ direction) with magnitude $B_{top} = \dfrac{\mu_0 i}{4\pi R}$.

The bottom semi-infinite segment carries current in the $+x$ direction. Its magnetic field at the origin is also directed out of the page ($+z$ direction) with magnitude $B_{bot} = \dfrac{\mu_0 i}{4\pi R}$.

The semi-circular arc carries current clockwise from $(0,R)$ to $(0,-R)$. Its magnetic field at the origin is directed into the page ($-z$ direction) with magnitude $B_{arc} = \dfrac{\mu_0 i}{4 R}$.

Taking the into-the-page direction as positive, the net magnetic field is $B_{net} = B_{arc} - (B_{top} + B_{bot}) = \dfrac{\mu_0 i}{4 R} - \left(\dfrac{\mu_0 i}{4\pi R} + \dfrac{\mu_0 i}{4\pi R}\right) = \dfrac{\mu_0 i}{4 R} \left[1 - \dfrac{2}{\pi}\right]$ directed into the page.

Step 2: Calculate the Lorentz force $\vec{F} = q(\vec{v} \times \vec{B})$.

The electron has charge $q = -e$. Its velocity $\vec{v}$ is to the left ($-x$ direction). The magnetic field $\vec{B}$ is into the page.

By the right-hand rule, the cross product $(\vec{v} \times \vec{B})$ points downwards ($-y$ direction). Since the electron is negatively charged, the force $\vec{F}$ is in the opposite direction, which is upwards ($+y$ direction), towards the top segment.

The magnitude of the force is $F = e v B_{net} = \dfrac{\mu_0 e v i}{4 R} \left[1 - \dfrac{2}{\pi}\right]$.

Answer: $\dfrac{\mu_0 e v i}{4 R} \left[1 - \dfrac{2}{\pi}\right]$ towards the top segment

104490.subject: Physics
104490.text: An astronomical telescope has an objective of focal length $150 \text{ cm}$ and an eyepiece of focal length $5 \text{ cm}$. It is initially focused on a distant star in normal adjustment. The observer then adjusts the eyepiece to refocus the telescope so that the final image forms at the least distance of distinct vision ($25 \text{ cm}$). What is the magnitude and direction of the displacement of the eyepiece?
104490.sol:
In normal adjustment, the final image is formed at infinity. The object for the eyepiece (the intermediate image formed by the objective) lies exactly at its principal focus.
$u_{e1} = f_e = 5 \text{ cm}$
The initial tube length is $L_1 = f_o + f_e = 150 + 5 = 155 \text{ cm}$.

When the telescope is adjusted so the final image is at the least distance of distinct vision ($v_e = -25 \text{ cm}$), we use the lens formula for the eyepiece to find the new object distance $u_{e2}$:
$\dfrac{1}{v_e} - \dfrac{1}{u_{e2}} = \dfrac{1}{f_e}$
$\dfrac{1}{-25} - \dfrac{1}{u_{e2}} = \dfrac{1}{5}$
$\dfrac{1}{u_{e2}} = -\dfrac{1}{25} - \dfrac{1}{5} = -\dfrac{6}{25}$
$u_{e2} = -\dfrac{25}{6} \text{ cm} \approx -4.17 \text{ cm}$

The new tube length is $L_2 = f_o + |u_{e2}| = 150 + \dfrac{25}{6} = 154.17 \text{ cm}$.

The displacement of the eyepiece is the difference in tube lengths:
$\Delta L = L_1 - L_2 = 5 - \dfrac{25}{6} = \dfrac{5}{6} \text{ cm}$.

Since the required tube length has decreased ($L_2 < L_1$), the eyepiece must be moved closer to the intermediate image, which means it is moved towards the objective.

Answer: $\dfrac{5}{6} \text{ cm}$ towards the objective

106410.text:
Match List I with List II regarding the radial probability distribution curves ($4\pi r^2 \psi^2$ vs $r$).

List I (Orbital)List II (Number of maxima/peaks)
(A) $2p$(I) $1$
(B) $3s$(II) $2$
(C) $4d$(III) $3$
(D) $4s$(IV) $4$

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
106410.sol:
The number of maxima (peaks) in the radial probability distribution curve ($4\pi r^2 \psi^2$ versus $r$) for an orbital is equal to the number of radial nodes plus one.
Number of peaks = $(n - l - 1) + 1 = n - l$.

Calculating the number of peaks for each given orbital:
(A) $2p$: $n = 2$, $l = 1$. Number of peaks = $2 - 1 = 1$. Matches with (I).
(B) $3s$: $n = 3$, $l = 0$. Number of peaks = $3 - 0 = 3$. Matches with (III).
(C) $4d$: $n = 4$, $l = 2$. Number of peaks = $4 - 2 = 2$. Matches with (II).
(D) $4s$: $n = 4$, $l = 0$. Number of peaks = $4 - 0 = 4$. Matches with (IV).

Therefore, the correct matching is (A)-(I), (B)-(III), (C)-(II), (D)-(IV).

Answer: (A)-(I), (B)-(III), (C)-(II), (D)-(IV)

106452.subject: Chemistry
106452.text: What is the maximum number of electrons in an atom that can have the principal quantum number $n = 4$ and the magnetic quantum number $m_l = +1$?
106452.sol:
For a given principal quantum number $n=4$, the possible values for the azimuthal quantum number $l$ are $0, 1, 2$, and $3$.

The magnetic quantum number $m_l$ can have values from $-l$ to $+l$. For an orbital to have $m_l = +1$, the value of $l$ must be at least $1$.

Thus, the subshells in the $n=4$ shell that contain an orbital with $m_l = +1$ are:
$l = 1$ ($4p$ subshell): contains one orbital with $m_l = +1$
$l = 2$ ($4d$ subshell): contains one orbital with $m_l = +1$
$l = 3$ ($4f$ subshell): contains one orbital with $m_l = +1$

There are a total of $3$ orbitals that satisfy the conditions $n=4$ and $m_l = +1$.

According to Pauli's exclusion principle, each orbital can accommodate a maximum of $2$ electrons (one with spin $+1/2$ and one with spin $-1/2$).

Maximum number of electrons = $3 \times 2 = 6$.

Answer: 6

107022.subject: Chemistry
107022.chapter: Classification of Elements and Periodicity in Properties
107022.text: The correct increasing order of first ionization enthalpy for the elements $\mathrm{Si}$, $\mathrm{P}$, $\mathrm{S}$, and $\mathrm{Cl}$ is:
107022.sol:
Across a period, the first ionization enthalpy generally increases with an increase in atomic number due to increasing effective nuclear charge.

However, Phosphorus ($\mathrm{P}$) has a stable half-filled $3p$ orbital configuration ($[\mathrm{Ne}] 3s^2 3p^3$), whereas Sulphur ($\mathrm{S}$) has a $3p^4$ configuration ($[\mathrm{Ne}] 3s^2 3p^4$). Removing an electron from the stable half-filled $p$-orbital of $\mathrm{P}$ requires more energy than removing the paired electron from the $p$-orbital of $\mathrm{S}$.

Thus, the first ionization enthalpy of $\mathrm{P}$ is greater than that of $\mathrm{S}$.

The correct increasing order is $\mathrm{Si} < \mathrm{S} < \mathrm{P} < \mathrm{Cl}$.

Answer: $\mathrm{Si} < \mathrm{S} < \mathrm{P} < \mathrm{Cl}$

108671.subject: Chemistry
108671.text:
Match List I with List II.

List I (Process)List II (Thermodynamic parameters)
A. Isothermal reversible expansion of an ideal gasI. $q = 0$, $w > 0$, $\Delta U > 0$
B. Adiabatic compressionII. $w = 0$, $q > 0$, $\Delta U > 0$
C. Heat supplied at constant volumeIII. $q = 0$, $w = 0$, $\Delta U = 0$
D. Free expansion of an ideal gas adiabaticallyIV. $\Delta U = 0$, $q > 0$, $w < 0$


Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
108671.sol:
According to the first law of thermodynamics, $\Delta U = q + w$.

A. For isothermal reversible expansion of an ideal gas, temperature is constant, so $\Delta U = 0$. Since it is an expansion, work is done by the system ($w < 0$). Therefore, $q = -w > 0$. (Matches IV)

B. For adiabatic compression, there is no heat exchange ($q = 0$). Compression means work is done on the system ($w > 0$). Therefore, $\Delta U = 0 + w > 0$. (Matches I)

C. When heat is supplied at constant volume, the process is isochoric ($\Delta V = 0$), so $w = 0$. Heat supplied means $q > 0$. Therefore, $\Delta U = q + 0 > 0$. (Matches II)

D. For free expansion of an ideal gas, the external pressure is zero, so $w = 0$. Since it is adiabatic, $q = 0$. Therefore, $\Delta U = 0 + 0 = 0$. (Matches III)

The correct matching is A-IV, B-I, C-II, D-III.

Answer: A-IV, B-I, C-II, D-III

111915.subject: Chemistry
111915.text: The heterolytic cleavage of the $\text{C}-\text{Br}$ bond in 2-bromo-2-methylbutane yields a carbocation intermediate. What is the number of hyperconjugative structures possible for this resulting carbocation?
111915.sol:
First, deduce the structure of the starting compound. 2-Bromo-2-methylbutane is $\text{CH}_3-\text{C}(\text{Br})(\text{CH}_3)-\text{CH}_2-\text{CH}_3$.

Heterolytic cleavage of the $\text{C}-\text{Br}$ bond results in the formation of the 2-methylbutan-2-yl carbocation: $\text{CH}_3-\text{C}^+(\text{CH}_3)-\text{CH}_2-\text{CH}_3$.

To find the number of hyperconjugative structures, count the number of $\alpha$-hydrogens attached to the carbons directly bonded to the positively charged carbon.

The $\alpha$-carbons are:
- C1 methyl group: 3 $\alpha$-hydrogens
- C2 methyl branch: 3 $\alpha$-hydrogens
- C3 methylene group: 2 $\alpha$-hydrogens

Total $\alpha$-hydrogens = $3 + 3 + 2 = 8$.

Therefore, 8 hyperconjugative structures are possible for this carbocation.

Answer: $8$

121593.text:
Read the following list of organisms:
Anabaena, Saccharomyces, Rhizobium, Gonyaulax, Trichoderma, Thermus aquaticus

How many of the given organisms are prokaryotic and belong to Kingdom Monera?
121593.sol:
Organisms belonging to Kingdom Monera are prokaryotes. They lack a true nucleus and membrane-bound organelles.

1. Anabaena is a cyanobacterium (blue-green alga) and belongs to Kingdom Monera.
2. Saccharomyces (yeast) is a unicellular eukaryote belonging to Kingdom Fungi.
3. Rhizobium is a symbiotic nitrogen-fixing bacterium, placed in Kingdom Monera.
4. Gonyaulax is a dinoflagellate, which is a unicellular eukaryote placed in Kingdom Protista.
5. Trichoderma is a fungus, hence eukaryotic.
6. Thermus aquaticus is a bacterium, hence prokaryotic and belongs to Kingdom Monera.

Therefore, there are three prokaryotic organisms in the given list: Anabaena, Rhizobium, and Thermus aquaticus.

Answer: Three

122700.sol: In monocotyledonous plants, the primary root is short lived and is replaced by a large number of roots. These roots originate from the base of the stem and constitute the fibrous root system, as seen in the wheat plant (Figure 5.2b). In some plants, like grass, Monstera and the banyan tree, roots arise from parts of the plant other than the radicle and are called adventitious roots (Figure 5.2c). The main functions of the root system are absorption of water and minerals from the soil, providing a proper anchorage to the plant parts, storing reserve food material and synthesis of plant growth regulators.

123822.subject: Botany
123822.text:
Match List I with List II:

List IList II
A. DiakinesisI. Resembles normal mitosis
B. PachyteneII. Reductional division
C. Meiosis IIII. Chromosomes are fully condensed
D. Meiosis IIIV. Recombination nodules appear

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
123822.sol:
According to NCERT, during diakinesis, the chromosomes are fully condensed and the meiotic spindle is assembled. Pachytene is characterised by the appearance of recombination nodules, the sites at which crossing over occurs between non-sister chromatids of homologous chromosomes. Meiosis I is a reductional division where homologous chromosomes separate, reducing the chromosome number to half. Meiosis II is an equational division that resembles normal mitosis, where sister chromatids separate.

Answer: A-III, B-IV, C-II, D-I

123905.subject: Botany
123905.text:
Match List-I with List-II.

List-IList-II
(A) Zygotene(I) Terminalisation of chiasmata
(B) Pachytene(II) Appearance of recombination nodules
(C) Diplotene(III) Formation of synaptonemal complex
(D) Diakinesis(IV) X-shaped structures called chiasmata

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
123905.sol:
The substages of prophase I in meiosis are characterized by specific chromosomal events:

(A) Zygotene is marked by the pairing of homologous chromosomes (synapsis) accompanied by the formation of the synaptonemal complex. (Matches III)

(B) Pachytene is characterized by the appearance of recombination nodules, which mark the sites where crossing over occurs between non-sister chromatids. (Matches II)

(C) Diplotene is recognized by the dissolution of the synaptonemal complex and the tendency of recombined homologous chromosomes to separate, except at the sites of crossing over, forming X-shaped structures called chiasmata. (Matches IV)

(D) Diakinesis is the final stage of prophase I and is marked by the terminalisation of chiasmata. (Matches I)

Therefore, the correct matching is (A)-(III), (B)-(II), (C)-(IV), (D)-(I).

Answer: (A)-(III), (B)-(II), (C)-(IV), (D)-(I)

124361.subject: Botany
124361.text:
Trace the correct chronological sequence of events for a newly synthesized secretory protein as it moves through the endomembrane system:

(A) Modification into glycoprotein in Golgi cisternae
(B) Synthesis by ribosomes on the rough endoplasmic reticulum
(C) Release from the trans face in secretory vesicles
(D) Packaging into transport vesicles at the endoplasmic reticulum
(E) Fusion of vesicles with the cis face of the Golgi apparatus

Choose the correct sequence from the options given below:
124361.sol:
The endomembrane system functions in a coordinated manner to synthesize, modify, and transport proteins.

First, the protein is synthesized by ribosomes attached to the rough endoplasmic reticulum (B).

Next, the newly synthesized proteins are packaged into transport vesicles at the endoplasmic reticulum (D).

These vesicles move towards the Golgi apparatus and fuse with its forming or cis face (E).

Inside the Golgi cisternae, the proteins are modified (e.g., glycosylation to form glycoproteins) (A).

Finally, the modified proteins are packaged into secretory vesicles and released from the maturing or trans face of the Golgi apparatus (C).

Therefore, the correct chronological sequence is (B), (D), (E), (A), (C).

Answer: (B), (D), (E), (A), (C)

options: occurs in Kranz anatomy where mesophyll have small chloroplast whereas bundle sheath have granal chloroplast
occurs in Kranz anatomy when mesophyll have small chloroplast where as bundle sheath have larger, agranal chloroplast

125756.sol: $\mathrm{C}_4$ plants have "Kranz type" anatomy. Vascular bundles are surrounded by bundle sheath cells. The chloroplasts are dimorphic. The cells of bundle sheath have very large chloroplasts. They lack grana and contain starch grains. They are centripetally arranged and mesophyll cells have small and agranal chloroplast.

125784.subject: Botany
125784.text: What tool is suggested for observing the stamens in detail?
125784.sol: the two parts of a typical stamen – the long and slender stalk called the filament, and the terminal generally bilobed structure called the anther. The proximal end of the filament is attached to the thalamus or the petal of the flower. The number and length of stamens are variable in flowers of different species. If you were to collect a stamen each from ten flowers (each from different species) and arrange them on a slide, you would be able to appreciate the large variation in size seen in nature. Careful observation of each stamen under a dissecting microscope and making neat diagrams would elucidate the range in shape and attachment of anthers in different flowers. A typical angiosperm anther is bilobed with each lobe having two theca, i.e., they are dithecous Often a longitudinal groove runs lengthwise separating the theca. Let us understand the various types of tissues and their organisation in the transverse section of an anther The bilobed nature of an anther is very distinct in the transverse section of the anther.

125804.subject: Botany
125804.text: How many wall layers generally surround a typical microsporangium?
125804.sol: The bilobed nature of an anther is very distinct in the transverse section of the anther. The anther is a four-sided (tetragonal) structure consisting of four microsporangia located at the corners, two in each lobe. The microsporangia develop further and become pollen sacs. They extend longitudinally all through the length of an anther and are packed with pollen grains. Structure of microsporangium: In a transverse section, a typical microsporangium appears near circular in outline. It is generally surrounded by four wall layers the epidermis, endothecium, middle layers and the tapetum. The outer three wall layers perform the function of protection and help in dehiscence of anther to release the pollen. The innermost wall layer is the tapetum. It nourishes the developing pollen grains. Cells of the tapetum possess dense cytoplasm and generally have more than one nucleus.

125907.subject: Botany
125907.text: How do flowers ensure they are visited frequently by animals?
options: By offering rewards such as nectar and pollen
125907.sol: Majority of insect-pollinated flowers are large, colourful, fragrant and rich in nectar. When the flowers are small, a number of flowers are clustered into an inflorescence to make them conspicuous. Animals are attracted to flowers by colour and/or fragrance. The flowers pollinated by flies and beetles secrete foul odours to attract these animals. To sustain animal visits, the flowers have to provide rewards to the animals. Nectar and pollen grains are the usual floral rewards. For harvesting the reward(s) from the flower the animal visitor comes in contact with the anthers and the stigma. The body of the animal gets a coating of pollen grains, which are generally sticky in animal pollinated flowers. When the animal carrying pollen on its body comes in contact with the stigma, it brings about pollination.

126267.subject: Botany
126267.text:
Given below are two statements: one is labelled as Assertion (A) and the other is labelled as Reason (R).

Assertion (A): Plants using abiotic pollinating agents like wind produce enormous amounts of pollen grains compared to the number of ovules available for pollination.
Reason (R): Pollen grains in wind-pollinated plants are heavy and sticky to ensure they successfully adhere to the stigma after being blown by the wind.

In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below:
options: Both (A) and (R) are correct and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
Both (A) and (R) are correct but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A)
(A) is correct but (R) is not correct
(A) is not correct but (R) is correct
126267.sol:
The Assertion is correct because pollination by abiotic agents (wind and water) is a chance event, leading to a massive loss of pollen grains. To compensate for this uncertainty, these flowers produce an enormous amount of pollen compared to the number of ovules.

The Reason is incorrect because pollen grains in wind-pollinated plants must be light and non-sticky so that they can be easily transported in wind currents. Heavy and sticky pollen grains are characteristic of insect-pollinated flowers.

Answer: (A) is correct but (R) is not correct

127899.subject: Zoology
127899.text: To which phylum do frogs belong?
127899.sol: Frogs can live both on land and in freshwater and belong to class Amphibia of phylum Chordata. The most common species of frog found in India is Rana tigrina. They do not have constant body temperature i.e., their body temperature varies with the temperature of the environment. Such animals are called cold blooded or poikilotherms. You might have also noticed changes in the colour of the frogs while they are in grasses and on dry land. They have the ability to change the colour to hide them from their enemies (camouflage). This protective coloration is called mimicry. You may also know that frogs are not seen during peak summer and winter. During this period they take shelter in deep burrows to protect them from extreme heat and cold. This is known as summer sleep (aestivation) and winter sleep (hibernation) respectively

128115.subject: Zoology
128115.text: Which of the following statements correctly describes the anatomical features specific to a male frog?
options: It possesses a copulatory pad on the first digit of the forelimb and a Bidder's canal in its kidneys.
It possesses a copulatory pad on the first digit of the hindlimb and vasa efferentia in its testes.
It possesses sound-producing vocal sacs and paired ovaries in its abdominal cavity.
It possesses a Bidder's canal in its kidneys and a copulatory pad on the second digit of the forelimb.
128115.sol:
In frogs, sexual dimorphism is prominent. Male frogs can be distinguished externally by the presence of sound-producing vocal sacs and a copulatory pad on the first digit of the forelimbs. Internally, male frogs possess a Bidder's canal in their kidneys, which is absent in females.

Option 2 is incorrect because the copulatory pad is on the forelimb, not the hindlimb.
Option 3 is incorrect because ovaries are a female reproductive structure.
Option 4 is incorrect because the copulatory pad is located on the first digit, not the second digit of the forelimb.

Answer: It possesses a copulatory pad on the first digit of the forelimb and a Bidder's canal in its kidneys.

128269.subject: Zoology
128269.text: What is the function of the hypothalamus in the endocrine system?
options: Regulation of secretion of pituitary hormones
128269.sol: As you know, the hypothalamus is the basal part of diencephalon, forebrain (Figure 19.1) and it regulates a wide spectrum of body functions. It contains several groups of neurosecretory cells called nuclei which produce hormones. These hormones regulate the synthesis and secretion of pituitary hormones. However, the hormones produced by hypothalamus are of two types, the releasing hormones (which stimulate secretion of pituitary hormones) and the inhibiting hormones (which inhibit secretions of pituitary hormones). For example a hypothalamic hormone called Gonadotrophin releasing hormone (GnRH) stimulates the pituitary synthesis and release of gonadotrophins. On the other hand, somatostatin from the hypothalamus inhibits the release of growth hormone from the pituitary. These hormones originating in the hypothalamic neurons, pass through axons and are released from their nerve endings. These hormones reach the pituitary gland through a portal circulatory system and regulate the functions of the anterior pituitary. The posterior pituitary is under the direct neural regulation of the hypothalamus.
128269.meta: What is the function of the hypothalamus in the endocrine system?

128279.subject: Zoology
128279.text: What is the function of neurohypophysis (pars nervosA)?
options: Produces growth hormone (GH), prolactin (PRL), thyroid stimulating hormone (TSH), adrenocorticotrophic hormone (ACTH), luteinizing hormone (LH) and follicle stimulating hormone (FSH)
Stores and releases oxytocin and vasopressin
128279.sol: The pituitary gland is located in a bony cavity called sella tursica and is attached to hypothalamus by a stalk (Figure 19.2). It is divided anatomically into an adenohypophysis and a neurohypophysis. Adenohypophysis consists of two portions, pars distalis and pars intermedia. The pars distalis region of pituitary, commonly called anterior pituitary, produces growth hormone (GH), prolactin (PRL), thyroid stimulating hormone (TSH), adrenocorticotrophic hormone (ACTH), luteinizing hormone (LH) and follicle stimulating hormone (FSH). Pars intermedia secretes only one hormone called melanocyte stimulating hormone (MSH). However, in humans, the pars intermedia is almost merged with pars distalis. Neurohypophysis (pars nervosa) also known as posterior pituitary, stores and releases two hormones called oxytocin and vasopressin, which are actually synthesised by the hypothalamus and are transported axonally to neurohypophysis.

128326.subject: Zoology
128326.text: What is the effect of parathyroid hormone (PTH) on bones?
128326.sol: Parathyroid hormone (PTH) increases the Ca2+ levels in the blood. PTH acts on bones and stimulates the process of bone resorption (dissolution/ demineralisation). PTH also stimulates reabsorption of Ca2+ by the renal tubules and increases Ca2+ absorption from the digested food. It is, thus, clear that PTH is a hypercalcemic hormone, i.e., it increases the blood Ca2+ levels. Along with TCT, it plays a significant role in calcium balance in the body. The thymus gland is a lobular structure located between lungs behind sternum on the ventral side of aorta. The thymus plays a major role in the development of the immune system. This gland secretes the peptide hormones called thymosins. Thymosins play a major role in the differentiation of T-lymphocytes, which provide cell-mediated immunity

129352.subject: Zoology
129352.text:
Match List I with List II regarding the components of a synapse:

List I List II
A. Synaptic vesicles 1. Contains specific receptors for neurotransmitters
B. Synaptic cleft 2. Fluid-filled space between neurons
C. Post-synaptic membrane 3. Pre- and post-synaptic membranes are in very close proximity
D. Electrical synapse 4. Store neurotransmitters

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
129352.sol:
Synaptic vesicles are found in the pre-synaptic axon terminal and store neurotransmitters (A-4).

The synaptic cleft is the fluid-filled space that separates the pre-synaptic and post-synaptic neurons in a chemical synapse (B-2).

The post-synaptic membrane contains specific receptors that bind to the released neurotransmitters (C-1).

In an electrical synapse, the membranes of pre- and post-synaptic neurons are in very close proximity, allowing direct flow of electric current (D-3).

Therefore, the correct matching is A-4, B-2, C-1, D-3.

Answer: A-4, B-2, C-1, D-3

129883.subject: Zoology
129883.text: What is the amount of CO₂ transported by RBCs in the blood?
129883.sol: Blood is the medium of transport for O2 and CO2. About 97 per cent of O2 is transported by RBCs in the blood. The remaining 3 per cent of O2 is carried in a dissolved state through the plasma. Nearly 20-25 per cent of CO2 is transported by RBCs whereas 70 per cent of it is carried as bicarbonate. About 7 per cent of CO2 is carried in a dissolved state through plasma.

130168.subject: Zoology
130168.text: What is the relationship between movements and locomotion?
options: All locomotions are movements but all movements are not locomotions
130168.sol:
The methods of locomotion performed by animals vary with their habitats and the demand of the situation, but the main purpose is to search for food, shelter, mate, suitable breeding grounds, favourable climatic conditions, or to escape from enemies/predators. The observations suggest that movements and locomotion cannot be studied separately and the two may be linked by stating that all locomotions are movements but all movements are not locomotions.

Movement is one of the significant features of living beings and animals and plants exhibit a wide range of movements.

130228.text: What is the function of myoglobin in muscles?
options: It generates energy for ATP production
It helps in cross bridge formation
It regulates the release of calcium ions
130228.sol: Muscle contraction is initiated by a signal sent by the central nervous system (CNS) via a motor neuron.The junction between a motor neuron and the sarcolemma of the muscle fibre is called the neuromuscular junction or motor-end plate.When a neural signal reaches the neuromuscular junction, it releases a neurotransmitter (Acetylcholine) which generates an action potential in the sarcolemma.Muscle contains a red coloured oxygen-storing pigment called myoglobin. Myoglobin stores oxygen and helps muscles in producing energy.Muscle contraction is powered by the hydrolysis of ATP, which provides energy for the cross bridge formation and breakage during muscle contraction.

130310.subject: Zoology
130310.text:
Match the following taking help from diagram shown:




Column A Column B Meromyosin a) Has active binding sites. Globular actin b) monomeric unit of myosin protein Globular Head c) monomeric unit of actin protein
130310.sol: Each actin (thin) filament is made of two ‘F’ (filamentous) actins helically wound to each other. Each ‘F’ actin is a polymer of monomeric ‘G’ (Globular) actins. Two filaments of another protein, tropomyosin also run close to the ‘F’ actins throughout its length. A complex protein Troponin is distributed at regular intervals on the tropomyosin. In the resting state a subunit of troponin masks the active binding sites for myosin on the actin filaments. Each myosin (thick) filament is also a polymerised protein. Many monomeric proteins called Meromyosins constitute one thick filament. Each meromyosin has two important parts, a globular head with a short arm and a tail, the former being called the heavy meromyosin (HMM) and the latter, the light meromyosin (LMM). The HMM component, i.e.; the head and short arm projects outwards at regular distance and angle from each other from the surface of a polymerised myosin filament and is known as cross arm. The globular head is an active ATPase enzyme and has binding sites for ATP and active sites for actin.

130818.text: The most important component of the oral contraceptive pills is
130818.sol: Use of contraceptive pills is a widespread form of birth control. Contraceptive pills contain oestrogen and progesterone. In the absence of FSH, the ovarian follicles do not ripen and ovulation does not occur in the absence of LH .

132035.text: What did humans do with the variations present in wild populations?
options: They selectively bred and selected for organisms with desirable characters
They studied them without using them
132035.sol: Humans knew from as early as 8000-1000 B.C. that one of the causes of variation was hidden in sexual reproduction. They exploited the variations that were naturally present in the wild populations of plants and animals to selectively breed and select for organisms that possessed desirable characters. For example, through artificial selection and domestication from ancestral wild cows, we have well-known Indian breeds, e.g., Sahiwal cows in Punjab. We must, however, recognise that though our ancestors knew about the inheritance of characters and variation, they had very little idea about the scientific basis of these phenomena.

134140.subject: Zoology
134140.text: Can ELISA detect mutations in genes in suspected cancer patients?
134140.sol: You know that for effective treatment of a disease, early diagnosis and understanding its pathophysiology is very important. Using conventional methods of diagnosis (serum and urine analysis, etc.) early detection is not possible. Recombinant DNA technology, Polymerase Chain Reaction (PCR) and Enzyme Linked Immuno-sorbent Assay (ELISA) are some of the techniques that serve the purpose of early diagnosis. Presence of a pathogen (bacteria, viruses, etc.) is normally suspected only when the pathogen has produced a disease symptom. By this time the concentration of pathogen is already very high in the body. However, very low concentration of a bacteria or virus (at a time when the symptoms of the disease are not yet visible) can be detected by amplification of their nucleic acid by PCR. Can you explain how PCR can detect very low amounts of DNA? PCR is now routinely used to detect HIV in suspected AIDS patients. It is being used to detect mutations in genes in suspected cancer patients too. It is a powerful techqnique to identify many other genetic disorders. A single stranded DNA or RNA, tagged with a radioactive molecule (probe) is allowed to hybridise to its complementary DNA in a clone of cells followed by detection using autoradiography. The clone having the mutated gene will hence not appear on the photographic film, because the probe will not have complementarity with the mutated gene. ELISA is based on the principle of antigen-antibody interaction. Infection by pathogen can be detected by the presence of antigens (proteins, glycoproteins, etc.) or by detecting the antibodies synthesized against the pathogen.
134140.meta: Can ELISA detect mutations in genes in suspected cancer patients?

134708.subject: Zoology
134708.text:
The DNA polymerase isolated from the bacterium Thermus aquaticus is widely used in Polymerase Chain Reaction (PCR). During the PCR cycle, this enzyme must survive the high temperature of step X without denaturing, and it actively synthesizes the new DNA strand during step Y.

Identify step X and step Y.
134708.sol:
In a Polymerase Chain Reaction (PCR), the first step is Denaturation (step X), where the double-stranded DNA is heated to a high temperature (around $94^{\circ}\text{C}$) to separate the strands. The DNA polymerase isolated from Thermus aquaticus (Taq polymerase) is thermostable and remains active despite this high temperature.

The third step is Extension (step Y), where the Taq polymerase actively adds nucleotides to the primers to synthesize the new complementary DNA strand at an optimal temperature of around $72^{\circ}\text{C}$.

Thus, step X is Denaturation and step Y is Extension.

Answer: X - Denaturation, Y - Extension

In a sparged stirred-tank bioreactor, sterile air bubbles are sparged through the liquid culture.

According to NCERT, the primary advantage of sparging air bubbles is that it significantly increases the surface area for oxygen transfer, ensuring that aerobic microbes receive adequate oxygen for optimal growth.

135081.text: For assessing impacts of any biotic or abiotic factor on population growth, which parameter is chosen?
135081.sol: Then the population grows in an exponential or geometric fashion. If in a population of size N, the birth rates (not total number but per capita births) are represented as b and death rates (again, per capita death rates) as d, then the increase or decrease in N during a unit time period t (dN/dt) will be dN/dt = (b – d) × NLet (b–d) = r, thendN/dt = rNThe r in this equation is called the ‘<mark>intrinsic rate of natural increase’ and is a very important parameter chosen for assessing impacts of any biotic or abiotic factor on population growth.</mark> To give you some idea about the magnitude of r values, for the Norway rat the r is 0.015, and for the flour beetle it is 0.12. In 1981, the r value for the human population in India was 0.0205.

135145.subject: Zoology
135145.text: What does Gause’s ‘Competitive Exclusion Principle’ state?
options: Two species will always coexist if resources are not limiting
Two closely related species competing for the same resources will eventually co-exist
Two closely related species cannot coexist indefinitely if competing for the same resources
Resource availability has no effect on species competition
135145.sol: <mark>Gause’s ‘Competitive Exclusion Principle’ states that two closely related species competing for the same resources cannot coexist indefinitely and the competitively inferior one will be eliminated eventually</mark>. This may be true if resources are limited, but not otherwise. More recent studies do not support such gross generalizations about competition. While they do not rule out the occurrence of interspecific competition in nature, they point out that species facing competition might evolve mechanisms that promote coexistence rather than exclusion. One such mechanism is ‘resource partitioning’. If two species compete for the same resource, they could avoid competition by choosing, for instance, different times for feeding or different foraging patterns. MacArthur showed that five closely related species of warblers living on the same tree were able to avoid competition and co-exist due to behavioral differences in their foraging activities.

135450.text: Assertion : Some marine animals find it difficult to live in fresh water and vice versa.Reason : Some animals can tolerate a narrow salinity range, while others can tolerate a wide salinity range.
options: If both assertion and reason are true and reason is the correct explanation of assertion
If both assertion and reason are true but reason is not the correct explanation of assertion
If assertion is true but reason is false
If both assertion and reason are false
135450.sol: For aquatic organism salt concentration (measured as salinity in parts per thousand) is a major factor for their survival. Salinity of different aquatic habitats varies greatly. It is less than 5 per thousand parts, in inland waters, 30-35 per thousand parts in the sea and more than 100 per thousand parts in some hypersaline lagoons. Many fresh water animals cannot live for long in sea water and vice versa because of the osmotic problems they would face due to the change in relative tonicity of the surrounding water with cytoplasm. It may result into endosmosis or exosmosis according to the conditions. The tolerance of organisms to the salinity range varies. Some organisms are tolerant of a wide range of salinities and are called euryhaline e.g. salmon, while some can tolerate only a narrow range of salinity i.e., stenohaline e.g., shark.

303765.subject: Physics
303765.text: A long narrow horizontal slit is placed $1 \text{ mm}$ above a horizontal plane mirror. The interference pattern formed by the light arriving directly from the slit and the light arriving after reflection is viewed on a screen placed $1.0 \text{ m}$ away from the slit. If the mirror reflects exactly $64\%$ of the incident light energy, determine the ratio of the maximum intensity to the minimum intensity in the observed interference pattern.
303765.sol:
Let the intensity of the light arriving directly from the slit be $I_1 = I$.

Since the mirror reflects $64\%$ of the incident light energy, the intensity of the light arriving after reflection is $I_2 = 0.64 I$.

The maximum intensity in the interference pattern is given by $I_\max = (\sqrt{I_1} + \sqrt{I_2})^2$.

The minimum intensity in the interference pattern is given by $I_\min = (\sqrt{I_1} - \sqrt{I_2})^2$.

The ratio of the maximum intensity to the minimum intensity is:

$\dfrac{I_\max}{I_\min} = \left( \dfrac{\sqrt{I_1} + \sqrt{I_2}}{\sqrt{I_1} - \sqrt{I_2}} \right)^2$

Substituting the values of $I_1$ and $I_2$:

$\dfrac{I_\max}{I_\min} = \left( \dfrac{\sqrt{I} + \sqrt{0.64 I}}{\sqrt{I} - \sqrt{0.64 I}} \right)^2$

$\dfrac{I_\max}{I_\min} = \left( \dfrac{1 + 0.8}{1 - 0.8} \right)^2$

$\dfrac{I_\max}{I_\min} = \left( \dfrac{1.8}{0.2} \right)^2 = (9)^2 = 81$

Thus, the ratio is $81 : 1$.

303832.subject: Physics
303832.text: A source emits light of wavelengths $555 \text{ nm}$ and $600 \text{ nm}$. The radiant flux of the $555 \text{ nm}$ part is $40 \text{ W}$ while that of the $600 \text{ nm}$ part is $30 \text{ W}$. The relative luminosity at $600 \text{ nm}$ is $0.6$. Determine the total luminous flux.
303832.sol:
The total luminous flux is the sum of the luminous fluxes for each wavelength.

The luminous flux for a given wavelength is calculated as $\Phi_v = 685 \times V(\lambda) \times \Phi_e(\lambda)$, where $V(\lambda)$ is the relative luminosity and $\Phi_e(\lambda)$ is the radiant flux.

At $555 \text{ nm}$, the relative luminosity is maximum, so $V(555 \text{ nm}) = 1$.

Luminous flux for the $555 \text{ nm}$ part:

$\Phi_{v1} = 685 \times 1 \times 40 = 27400 \text{ lumen}$

For the $600 \text{ nm}$ part, the relative luminosity is given as $V(600 \text{ nm}) = 0.6$.

Luminous flux for the $600 \text{ nm}$ part:

$\Phi_{v2} = 685 \times 0.6 \times 30 = 12330 \text{ lumen}$

Total luminous flux:

$\Phi_v = \Phi_{v1} + \Phi_{v2} = 27400 + 12330 = 39730 \text{ lumen}$

303855.subject: Physics
303855.text: Particles having masses of $1 \text{ g}$, $2 \text{ g}$, $3 \text{ g}$, ..., $100 \text{ g}$ are placed at the marks $1 \text{ cm}$, $2 \text{ cm}$, $3 \text{ cm}$, ..., $100 \text{ cm}$ respectively on a metre scale. Determine the moment of inertia of this system of particles about the perpendicular bisector of the metre scale.
303855.sol:
The perpendicular bisector of a metre scale passes through its midpoint at $50 \text{ cm}$.

The moment of inertia of the system about this axis is given by:

$I = \sum_{i=1}^{100} m_i r_i^2$

where $m_i = i \text{ g}$ and the distance from the axis is $r_i = |i - 50| \text{ cm}$.

$I = \sum_{i=1}^{100} i (i - 50)^2$

Let $j = i - 50$. As $i$ varies from $1$ to $100$, $j$ varies from $-49$ to $50$.

$I = \sum_{j=-49}^{50} (j + 50) j^2 = \sum_{j=-49}^{50} j^3 + 50 \sum_{j=-49}^{50} j^2$

Since $j^3$ is an odd power, the sum of symmetric terms is zero, giving $\sum_{j=-49}^{49} j^3 = 0$.

$\sum_{j=-49}^{50} j^3 = 50^3 = 125000$

For the second term, using the sum of squares formula $\sum_{j=1}^{n} j^2 = \dfrac{n(n+1)(2n+1)}{6}$:

$\sum_{j=-49}^{50} j^2 = 50^2 + 2 \sum_{j=1}^{49} j^2$

$\sum_{j=1}^{49} j^2 = \dfrac{49 \times 50 \times 99}{6} = 40425$

$\sum_{j=-49}^{50} j^2 = 2500 + 2(40425) = 83350$

Substituting these values back into the equation for $I$:

$I = 125000 + 50(83350) = 125000 + 4167500 = 4292500 \text{ g cm}^2$

Converting the units to $\text{kg m}^2$:

$I = 4292500 \times 10^{-3} \text{ kg} \times (10^{-2} \text{ m})^2$

$I = 4292500 \times 10^{-7} \text{ kg m}^2 = 0.42925 \text{ kg m}^2$

Rounding to two decimal places, we get $0.43 \text{ kg m}^2$.

Answer: $0.43 \text{ kg m}^2$

303967.text: As illustrated in the figure, a block of mass $m_1$ is fastened to a spring on an incline of angle $\theta$, and a block of mass $m_2$ is placed against it. Determine the compression of the spring when the system is in its equilibrium position.
303967.sol:
Consider the blocks $m_1$ and $m_2$ as a single system of mass $(m_1 + m_2)$.

In the equilibrium position, the net force acting on the system along the inclined plane is zero.

The downward force along the incline due to gravity is $(m_1 + m_2)g \sin\theta$.

The upward force along the incline due to the compressed spring is $kx$, where $x$ is the compression of the spring.

Equating these forces:

$kx = (m_1 + m_2)g \sin\theta$

$x = \dfrac{(m_1 + m_2)g \sin\theta}{k}$

303986.subject: Physics
303986.text: As shown in the figure, the left block travels at a speed $v$ towards the right block, which is placed in equilibrium. All collisions that occur are elastic and the surfaces are frictionless. Determine the time period of the periodic motions of the two blocks. Neglect the widths of the blocks.
303986.sol:
Let the cycle begin when the left block moves from the left wall towards the right block with velocity $v$.

The distance to the right block is $L$. The time taken by the left block to reach the right block is:
$t_1 = \dfrac{L}{v}$

Since the collision is perfectly elastic and both blocks have the same mass $m$, they exchange their velocities upon impact. The left block comes to rest, and the right block acquires the velocity $v$ towards the right.

The right block then compresses the spring, comes to a momentary halt, and returns to its equilibrium position. This motion constitutes exactly half of a simple harmonic oscillation. The time taken for this half-cycle is:
$t_2 = \dfrac{1}{2} \left( 2\pi \sqrt{\dfrac{m}{k}} \right) = \pi \sqrt{\dfrac{m}{k}}$

When the right block returns to its equilibrium position, it has a velocity $v$ directed towards the left. It then collides elastically with the stationary left block. Velocities are exchanged once again: the right block comes to rest, and the left block acquires a velocity $v$ towards the left.

The left block travels the distance $L$ back to the left wall. The time taken for this return journey is:
$t_3 = \dfrac{L}{v}$

Upon reaching the left wall, the left block collides elastically with it and rebounds with velocity $v$ towards the right. This brings the system back to its exact initial state, completing one full cycle.

The total time period $T$ of the periodic motion is the sum of these time intervals:
$T = t_1 + t_2 + t_3$

$T = \dfrac{L}{v} + \pi \sqrt{\dfrac{m}{k}} + \dfrac{L}{v}$

$T = \pi \sqrt{\dfrac{m}{k}} + \dfrac{2L}{v}$

304101.text: Determine the bulk modulus of air using the given data for a sound wave of wavelength $35 \text{ cm}$ travelling in air. The pressure at a specific point fluctuates between $(1.0 \times 10^5 \pm 14) \text{ Pa}$, and the particles of the air undergo simple harmonic motion with an amplitude of $5.5 \times 10^{-6} \text{ m}$.
304101.sol:
The pressure amplitude $\Delta P_m$ of a sound wave is related to the bulk modulus $B$, the wave number $k$, and the displacement amplitude $A$ by the relation:

$\Delta P_m = B k A$

The wave number $k$ is given by $k = \dfrac{2\pi}{\lambda}$. Substituting this into the equation gives:

$\Delta P_m = B \left(\dfrac{2\pi}{\lambda}\right) A$

Rearranging for the bulk modulus $B$:

$B = \dfrac{\Delta P_m \lambda}{2\pi A}$

Given the values:
Pressure amplitude, $\Delta P_m = 14 \text{ Pa}$
Wavelength, $\lambda = 35 \text{ cm} = 0.35 \text{ m}$
Displacement amplitude, $A = 5.5 \times 10^{-6} \text{ m}$

Substituting these values into the formula:

$B = \dfrac{14 \times 0.35}{2 \times \pi \times 5.5 \times 10^{-6}}$

Using $\pi \approx \dfrac{22}{7}$:

$B = \dfrac{4.9}{11 \times \dfrac{22}{7} \times 10^{-6}}$

$B = \dfrac{4.9 \times 7}{242 \times 10^{-6}}$

$B = \dfrac{34.3}{242} \times 10^6$

$B \approx 1.41 \times 10^5 \text{ Pa}$

Rounding to two significant figures, we get $1.4 \times 10^5 \text{ Pa}$.

304205.text: A stretched string carries a wave in the positive $x$-direction with a wave speed of $v$. The displacement of the particle at $x = 0$ is described by $f(t) = A \sin(t/T)$. Determine the wave equation.
304205.sol:
For a wave traveling in the positive $x$-direction with speed $v$, the displacement $f(x, t)$ at any position $x$ and time $t$ is given by the displacement at $x = 0$ at an earlier time $t - \dfrac{x}{v}$.

Given the displacement at $x = 0$ is $f(t) = A \sin \left(\dfrac{t}{T}\right).

Substituting $t$ with $t - $\dfrac{x}{v} gives the wave equation:

$f(x, t) = A \sin \left(\dfrac{t - \dfrac{x}{v}}{T}\right)$

$f(x, t) = A \sin \left(\dfrac{t}{T} - \dfrac{x}{vT}\right)

304487.text: Assume a quantity $x$ can be dimensionally expressed in terms of $M$, $L$, and $T$, such that $[x] = M^a L^b T^c$. The quantity mass
options: may be expressed in terms of $L$, $T$, and $x$ if $a \neq 0$
can never be dimensionally expressed in terms of $L$, $T$, and $x$
can always be dimensionally expressed in terms of $L$, $T$, and $x$
may be expressed in terms of $L$, $T$, and $x$ if $a = 0$
304487.sol:
Given $[x] = M^a L^b T^c$

Rearranging the terms to express $M$ in terms of $x$, $L$, and $T$:

$M^a = [x] L^{-b} T^{-c}$

$M = [x]^{1/a} L^{-b/a} T^{-c/a}$

For this relation to be valid, the exponent $1/a$ must be defined, which requires $a \neq 0$.

Therefore, mass may be expressed in terms of $L$, $T$, and $x$ if $a \neq 0$.

305790.text: Using the figure, determine the boiling point of methyl alcohol at $1 \text{ atm}$ ($760 \text{ mm}$ of mercury) and at $0.5 \text{ atm}$.
305790.sol:
The boiling point of a liquid is the temperature at which its vapour pressure equals the external atmospheric pressure.

For methyl alcohol, the normal boiling point at $1 \text{ atm}$ ($760 \text{ mm}$ of Hg) is known to be $65^\circ \text{C}$.

When the external pressure is reduced to $0.5 \text{ atm}$ ($380 \text{ mm}$ of Hg), the boiling point decreases. Based on the standard vapour pressure curve of methyl alcohol, the temperature at which its vapour pressure is $0.5 \text{ atm}$ is $48^\circ \text{C}$.

Thus, the boiling points are $65^\circ \text{C}$ and $48^\circ \text{C}$ respectively.

306038.subject: Physics
306038.text: A short magnet in an oscillation magnetometer oscillates with a time period of $0.10 \text{ s}$ at a location where the earth's horizontal magnetic field is $24 \mu\text{T}$. A downward current of $18 \text{ A}$ is set up in a vertical wire positioned $20 \text{ cm}$ east of the magnet. Determine the new time period.
306038.sol:
The magnetic field produced by the vertical wire at the position of the magnet is given by:

$B_{\text{wire}} = \dfrac{\mu_0 I}{2\pi r}$

Substituting the given values:

$B_{\text{wire}} = \dfrac{4\pi \times 10^{-7} \times 18}{2\pi \times 0.20} = 18 \times 10^{-6} \text{ T} = 18 \mu\text{T}$

By the right-hand grip rule, for a downward current in a wire located east of the magnet, the magnetic field at the magnet's position points North. Since the Earth's horizontal magnetic field $B_H$ also points North, the two magnetic fields add up.

The net magnetic field is:

$B_{\text{net}} = B_H + B_{\text{wire}} = 24 \mu\text{T} + 18 \mu\text{T} = 42 \mu\text{T}$

The time period of an oscillation magnetometer is given by $T = 2\pi \sqrt{\dfrac{I}{MB}}$, which implies $T \propto \dfrac{1}{\sqrt{B}}$.

Therefore, the new time period $T_2$ is:

$\dfrac{T_2}{T_1} = \sqrt{\dfrac{B_1}{B_2}}$

$T_2 = 0.10 \times \sqrt{\dfrac{24}{42}} = 0.10 \times \sqrt{\dfrac{4}{7}}$

$T_2 \approx 0.10 \times 0.756 = 0.0756 \text{ s} \approx 0.076 \text{ s}$

306238.subject: Physics
306238.text: At a certain time, a specific sample of a radioactive material decays at the rate of $500$ per second. After $50 \text{ minutes}$, the count rate falls to $200$ per second. Determine the half-life of the sample.
306238.sol:
The radioactive decay law is given by $A = A_0 e^{-\lambda t}$.

Given $A_0 = 500 \text{ s}^{-1}$ and $A = 200 \text{ s}^{-1}$ at $t = 50 \text{ min}$.

Substituting the values:

$200 = 500 e^{-50\lambda}$

$e^{50\lambda} = \dfrac{500}{200} = 2.5$

Taking the natural logarithm on both sides:

$50\lambda = \ln 2.5$

$\lambda = \dfrac{\ln 2.5}{50}$

The half-life $T_{1/2}$ is given by:

$T_{1/2} = \dfrac{\ln 2}{\lambda} = \dfrac{50 \ln 2}{\ln 2.5}$

Using $\log_{10} 2 \approx 0.301$ and $\log_{10} 2.5 = \log_{10}\left(\dfrac{10}{4}\right) = 1 - 2\log_{10} 2 \approx 0.398$:

$T_{1/2} = 50 \times \dfrac{0.301}{0.398} \approx 37.8 \text{ min}$

Rounding to the nearest integer, we get $38 \text{ min}$.

306472.subject: Physics
306472.text: A bar magnet is released from rest along the central axis of a very long, vertical copper tube. After some time elapses, the magnet
options: will travel with a nearly constant speed
will come to rest inside the tube
will move with an acceleration equal to $g$
306472.sol:
When a bar magnet falls through a vertical copper tube, the magnetic flux linked with the tube changes continuously.

This changing magnetic flux induces eddy currents in the walls of the copper tube.

According to Lenz's law, the direction of these induced eddy currents is such that they oppose the downward motion of the magnet.

The upward opposing magnetic force is proportional to the velocity of the falling magnet. As the speed of the magnet increases, the opposing force also increases.

Eventually, the upward magnetic force exactly balances the downward gravitational force acting on the magnet.

At this point, the net force on the magnet becomes zero, and its acceleration becomes zero.

Thereafter, the magnet continues to fall with a nearly constant terminal speed.

309073.text:
Identify the major product of the following reaction sequence:

$\xrightarrow[\text{(ii) Catalytic } \mathrm{H}^{+}\text{, heat}]{\text{(i) Excess } \mathrm{CH}_3\mathrm{MgBr}\text{, then } \mathrm{H}_3\mathrm{O}^{+}}$ ?
309073.sol:
The given reactant is a lactone, specifically 3,3-dimethylisobenzofuran-1(3H)-one.

In the first step, it reacts with an excess of the Grignard reagent, methylmagnesium bromide ($\text{CH}_3\text{MgBr}$). The Grignard reagent attacks the electrophilic carbonyl carbon of the ester group. Two equivalents of $\text{CH}_3\text{MgBr}$ are consumed per lactone molecule. The first equivalent opens the lactone ring to form a ketone intermediate bearing a tertiary alkoxide group. The second equivalent then attacks the newly formed ketone carbonyl.

Subsequent acidic workup ($\text{H}_3\text{O}^+$) protonates the resulting di-alkoxide intermediate to yield a diol, 1,2-bis(2-hydroxypropan-2-yl)benzene. This intermediate has an ortho-disubstituted benzene ring with two $-\text{C}(\text{CH}_3)_2\text{OH}$ groups.

In the second step, the diol is treated with a catalytic amount of acid ($\text{H}^+$) and heated. This promotes an intramolecular acid-catalyzed dehydration reaction. One of the tertiary hydroxyl groups is protonated and eliminates as a water molecule, generating a relatively stable tertiary benzylic carbocation.

The second hydroxyl group acts as an internal nucleophile and attacks this carbocation to close the ring. After the loss of a proton, a new five-membered cyclic ether is formed.

The final major product is 1,1,3,3-tetramethyl-1,3-dihydroisobenzofuran, which corresponds to the structure shown in option (2).

309256.subject: Chemistry
309256.text:
Identify the starting material (?) in the given reaction sequence:

? $\xrightarrow[\text{(ii) Vinyl lithium, then } \mathrm{H}_3\mathrm{O}^+, \Delta]{\text{(i) CuCN}}$
309256.sol:
The given reaction sequence involves two main steps to form phenyl vinyl ketone.

The starting material reacts with $\text{CuCN}$. Among the given options, the benzenediazonium cation (Option A) undergoes the Sandmeyer reaction with $\text{CuCN}$ to form benzonitrile ($\text{Ph-CN}$).
$\text{Ph-N}_2^+ + \text{CuCN} \rightarrow \text{Ph-CN} + \text{N}_2$

Benzonitrile reacts with vinyl lithium ($\text{CH}_2\text{=CH-Li}$). The nucleophilic vinyl group attacks the electrophilic carbon of the nitrile, forming an imine salt intermediate.
$\text{Ph-CN} + \text{CH}_2\text{=CH-Li} \rightarrow \text{Ph-C(=NLi)-CH=CH}_2$

Acidic hydrolysis ($\text{H}_3\text{O}^+, \Delta$) of the imine salt converts it into the corresponding ketone, which is phenyl vinyl ketone (the given product).
$\text{Ph-C(=NLi)-CH=CH}_2 \xrightarrow{\text{H}_3\text{O}^+} \text{Ph-C(=O)-CH=CH}_2$

Thus, the correct starting material is the benzenediazonium cation.

309327.text:
Consider the following statements about the given disaccharide:



I. Both rings are in the pyranose form.
II. It is a reducing sugar.
III. It is a non-reducing sugar.

Choose the correct option:
309327.sol:
Based on the given structure of the disaccharide:

1. Both rings are six-membered rings containing one oxygen atom. This indicates that both monosaccharide units are in the pyranose form. Therefore, statement I is correct.

2. The rightmost ring has a free hydroxyl ($-OH$) group at its anomeric carbon (C1). This means it contains a hemiacetal group, which can open up in an aqueous solution to form a free aldehyde group. Because of this, the disaccharide can act as a reducing agent and is classified as a reducing sugar. Therefore, statement II is correct, and statement III is incorrect.

Since statements I and II are correct, the correct option is (C).

Answer: I and II only

309384.subject: Chemistry
309384.text: In the cyclic structure of D-fructofuranose, which carbon atom is the anomeric carbon?
309384.sol:
D-fructose is a ketohexose with the ketone group located at the C-2 position in its open-chain structure.

During the formation of the cyclic D-fructofuranose structure, the hydroxyl group at C-5 undergoes an intramolecular nucleophilic addition to the carbonyl carbon at C-2, forming a hemiketal ring.

The carbonyl carbon (C-2) becomes a new chiral center in this cyclic structure. This newly formed chiral center is known as the anomeric carbon.

Therefore, the anomeric carbon in D-fructofuranose is C-2.

Answer: C-2

309409.subject: Chemistry
309409.text:
Identify the major product formed in the following reaction sequence:

(i) $\mathrm{SOCl}_{2}$
(ii) $\mathrm{CH}_{3}\mathrm{CH}_{2}\mathrm{OH}, \mathrm{H}^{+}$
309409.sol:
The given reactant is benzoic acid ($\mathrm{C}_{6}\mathrm{H}_{5}\mathrm{COOH}$).

In the first step, benzoic acid reacts with thionyl chloride ($\mathrm{SOCl}_{2}$) to undergo a nucleophilic acyl substitution, replacing the hydroxyl group with a chloride ion to form benzoyl chloride.
$\mathrm{C}_{6}\mathrm{H}_{5}\mathrm{COOH} + \mathrm{SOCl}_{2} \rightarrow \mathrm{C}_{6}\mathrm{H}_{5}\mathrm{COCl} + \mathrm{SO}_{2} + \mathrm{HCl}$

In the second step, benzoyl chloride reacts with ethanol ($\mathrm{CH}_{3}\mathrm{CH}_{2}\mathrm{OH}$) in an acidic medium. This is an alcoholysis reaction where the acid chloride is converted into an ester.
$\mathrm{C}_{6}\mathrm{H}_{5}\mathrm{COCl} + \mathrm{CH}_{3}\mathrm{CH}_{2}\mathrm{OH} \rightarrow \mathrm{C}_{6}\mathrm{H}_{5}\mathrm{COOCH}_{2}\mathrm{CH}_{3} + \mathrm{HCl}$

The final major product is ethyl benzoate, which corresponds to the structure in option (C).

314760.text: Suppose $a, b$ are positive real numbers such that $a \sqrt{a}+b \sqrt{b}=183, a \sqrt{b}+b \sqrt{a}=182$. Find $\frac{9}{5}(a+b)$.
314760.sol:
$a \sqrt{a}+b \sqrt{b}=183$ and $a \sqrt{b}+b \sqrt{a}=182$ we have to find $\frac{9}{5}(a+b)$
Let $a=A^2, b=B^2$
$\begin{aligned}
& A^3+B^3=183 \ldots \ldots \ldots \ldots . \text { (i) } \\
& A^2 B+B^2 A=182 \ldots \ldots \ldots . . \text { (ii) } \\
& (1)+(2) \\
& A^3+B^3+3 A B(A+B)=183+3 \times 182 \\
& (A+B)^3=183+546 \\
& (A+B)^3=729 \\
& \Rightarrow A+B=9
\end{aligned}$
$\begin{aligned} & \text { from }(2) \rightarrow A B(A+B)=182 \\ & A B=\frac{182}{9} \\ & a+b=A^2+B^2=(A+B)^2-2 A B \\ & =81-\frac{364}{9}=\frac{365}{9} \\ & \frac{9}{5} \times \frac{365}{9}=73\end{aligned}$

6a104ffa8b46719ce7976d08.subject: Chemistry
6a104ffa8b46719ce7976d08.text: At a constant temperature, the Henry's law constants ($K_H$) for four gases $W, X, Y,$ and $Z$ in water are $35 \text{ kbar}$, $0.15 \text{ kbar}$, $76 \text{ kbar}$, and $1.67 \text{ kbar}$ respectively. The correct increasing order of their solubility in water at a given partial pressure is:
6a104ffa8b46719ce7976d08.sol:
According to Henry's law, $p = K_H x$, where $p$ is the partial pressure of the gas, $K_H$ is the Henry's law constant, and $x$ is the mole fraction of the gas in the solution (solubility).

At a constant partial pressure, $x = \dfrac{p}{K_H}$. Thus, solubility is inversely proportional to the Henry's law constant ($K_H$).

The given $K_H$ values are:
$K_H(W) = 35 \text{ kbar}$
$K_H(X) = 0.15 \text{ kbar}$
$K_H(Y) = 76 \text{ kbar}$
$K_H(Z) = 1.67 \text{ kbar}$

The decreasing order of $K_H$ values is $Y > W > Z > X$.

Therefore, the increasing order of solubility is $Y < W < Z < X$.

Answer: $Y < W < Z < X$

6a0e2775165ae1327797b371.text:
In an experiment to determine the specific resistance of a metallic wire, a student uses the relation $\rho = \dfrac{\pi V d^2}{4 I L}$, where $V$ is the potential difference across the wire, $I$ is the current, $d$ is the diameter, and $L$ is the length.

If the percentage errors in the measurement of $V, I, d$, and $L$ are $2\%, 1\%, 3\%$, and $2\%$ respectively, the maximum percentage error in the calculated value of $\rho$ will be
6a0e2775165ae1327797b371.sol:
Given the relation for specific resistance:

$\rho = \dfrac{\pi V d^2}{4 I L}$

The maximum percentage error in $\rho$ is given by the sum of the percentage errors of the individual quantities, multiplied by their respective powers:

$\dfrac{\Delta \rho}{\rho} \times 100 = \left( \dfrac{\Delta V}{V} + 2\dfrac{\Delta d}{d} + \dfrac{\Delta I}{I} + \dfrac{\Delta L}{L} \right) \times 100$

Substituting the given percentage errors:

$\dfrac{\Delta \rho}{\rho} \times 100 = 2\% + 2(3\%) + 1\% + 2\%$

$\dfrac{\Delta \rho}{\rho} \times 100 = 2\% + 6\% + 1\% + 2\% = 11\%$

Answer: $11\%$

6a0e2779165ae1327797b3d6.subject: Biology
6a0e2779165ae1327797b3d6.text: While examining the transverse section of an unidentified invertebrate, a student notices a distinct fluid-filled space between the body wall and the gut. However, the mesoderm does not form a continuous lining around this cavity; instead, it is present as scattered pouches between the ectoderm and endoderm. Based on this observation, which of the following organisms could this specimen be?
6a0e2779165ae1327797b3d6.sol:
The presence of a fluid-filled cavity between the body wall and the gut, where the mesoderm is present as scattered pouches between the ectoderm and endoderm, is characteristic of a pseudocoelom.

Animals possessing a pseudocoelom are called pseudocoelomates. This feature is a hallmark of the phylum Aschelminthes.

Among the given options, $Ancylostoma$ (hookworm) belongs to the phylum Aschelminthes and is a pseudocoelomate.

$Fasciola$ (Platyhelminthes) is an acoelomate.

$Pheretima$ (Annelida) is a true coelomate.

$Adamsia$ (Cnidaria) is diploblastic and lacks a coelom.

Answer: Ancylostoma

6a252ff198efbb6c17e929c9.subject: Chemistry
6a252ff198efbb6c17e929c9.text: According to molecular orbital theory, which of the following diatomic ions is predicted to have a bond order of zero and therefore does not exist?
6a252ff198efbb6c17e929c9.sol:
The total number of electrons in $\mathrm{C}_2^{2-}$ is $12 + 2 = 14$.

Bond order = $\dfrac{1}{2}(10 - 4) = 3$.

The total number of electrons in $\mathrm{N}_2^{2-}$ is $14 + 2 = 16$.

Bond order = $\dfrac{1}{2}(10 - 6) = 2$.

The total number of electrons in $\mathrm{O}_2^{2-}$ is $16 + 2 = 18$.

Bond order = $\dfrac{1}{2}(10 - 8) = 1$.

The total number of electrons in $\mathrm{F}_2^{2-}$ is $18 + 2 = 20$.

The molecular orbital configuration is $\sigma_{1s}^{2} \sigma^{*}_{1s}^{2} \sigma_{2s}^{2} \sigma^{*}_{2s}^{2} \sigma_{2p_z}^{2} \pi_{2p_x}^{2} \pi_{2p_y}^{2} \pi^{*}_{2p_x}^{2} \pi^{*}_{2p_y}^{2} \sigma^{*}_{2p_z}^{2}$.

Number of bonding electrons $N_b = 10$ and antibonding electrons $N_a = 10$.

Bond order = $\dfrac{1}{2}(N_b - N_a) = \dfrac{1}{2}(10 - 10) = 0$.

Since the bond order is zero, $\mathrm{F}_2^{2-}$ does not exist.

Answer: $\mathrm{F}_2^{2-}$

6a252ff498efbb6c17e92a16.subject: Biology
6a252ff498efbb6c17e92a16.text: Which of the following statements correctly describes the theory of spontaneous generation?
options: Life arises only from pre-existing living organisms.
Life came out of decaying and rotting matter like straw and mud.
The first form of life originated from non-living organic molecules.
Units of life were transferred to Earth from outer space.
6a252ff498efbb6c17e92a16.sol:
The theory of spontaneous generation states that life came out of decaying and rotting matter like straw, mud, etc.

The theory of biogenesis states that life arises only from pre-existing living organisms.

The theory of chemical evolution states that the first form of life originated from non-living organic molecules.

The theory of panspermia states that units of life called spores were transferred to Earth from outer space.

Answer: Life came out of decaying and rotting matter like straw and mud.

6a7a1ff86c73a9a4aed87a15.subject: Physics
6a7a1ff86c73a9a4aed87a15.text: A fixed mass of an ideal gas undergoes two distinct adiabatic expansion processes. Process A takes the gas from an initial state $(P_1, V_1)$ to a final state $(P_2, V_2)$. Process B takes the same gas from a different initial state $(P_3, V_3)$ to a final state $(P_4, V_4)$. It is observed that both processes start at the same initial temperature $T_1$ and end at the same final temperature $T_2$. If $W_A$ and $W_B$ represent the magnitudes of the work done by the gas in Process A and Process B respectively, which of the following relationships is correct?
options: Cannot be determined without knowing the exact values of pressures and volumes
6a7a1ff86c73a9a4aed87a15.sol:
For an adiabatic process, the heat exchange is zero ($Q = 0$).

According to the first law of thermodynamics, $Q = \Delta U + W$, which gives $W = -\Delta U$.

The change in internal energy for an ideal gas is given by $\Delta U = nC_v\Delta T$.

Since both processes involve the same fixed mass of the same ideal gas (same $n$ and $C_v$) and operate between the identical initial and final temperatures (same $\Delta T$), the change in internal energy is exactly the same for both processes.

Therefore, the magnitudes of the work done must be equal, yielding $W_A = W_B$.

Answer: $W_A = W_B$

6a7a1ff8204edf27976dd3e7.text: A transverse wave on a stretched string is described by the equation $y(x,t) = 0.05 \sin(40x - 800t)$, where $x$ and $y$ are in metres and $t$ is in seconds. If the linear mass density of the string is $5.0 \mathrm{~g/m}$, the tension in the string is :
6a7a1ff8204edf27976dd3e7.sol:
Comparing the given wave equation $y(x,t) = 0.05 \sin(40x - 800t)$ with the standard form $y(x,t) = A \sin(kx - \omega t)$, we get:
Angular frequency, $\omega = 800 \mathrm{~rad/s}$
Wave number, $k = 40 \mathrm{~rad/m}$

The wave speed $v$ is given by:
$v = \dfrac{\omega}{k} = \dfrac{800}{40} = 20 \mathrm{~m/s}$

The linear mass density of the string is:
$\mu = 5.0 \mathrm{~g/m} = 5.0 \times 10^{-3} \mathrm{~kg/m}$

The speed of a transverse wave on a stretched string is related to the tension $T$ by:
$v = \sqrt{\dfrac{T}{\mu}}$

Squaring both sides and solving for $T$:
$T = \mu v^{2}$
$T = (5.0 \times 10^{-3}) \times (20)^{2}$
$T = 5.0 \times 10^{-3} \times 400 = 2 \mathrm{~N}$

Answer: $2 \mathrm{~N}$

6a7a1ff88f2febac74bce19c.subject: Physics
6a7a1ff88f2febac74bce19c.text:
An AC voltage source $v = V_0 \sin(\omega t)$ is connected across a circuit. The resulting steady-state current is given by $i = I_0 \cos(\omega t)$.

Which of the following correctly describes the possible composition of the circuit?
options: Either a pure capacitor or an LC series circuit with $X_C > X_L$
Either a pure inductor or an LC series circuit with $X_L > X_C$
6a7a1ff88f2febac74bce19c.sol:
The given voltage is $v = V_0 \sin(\omega t)$.

The given current is $i = I_0 \cos(\omega t)$.

We can rewrite the current equation in terms of sine as $i = I_0 \sin\left(\omega t + \dfrac{\pi}{2}\right)$.

This shows that the current leads the voltage by a phase angle of $\dfrac{\pi}{2}$.

A phase lead of $\dfrac{\pi}{2}$ occurs in a purely capacitive circuit. This can be achieved either by a pure capacitor or by an LC series circuit where the capacitive reactance is greater than the inductive reactance ($X_C > X_L$).

Answer: Either a pure capacitor or an LC series circuit with $X_C > X_L$

6a7a1ff8af9e6877547963da.text: An electromagnetic wave is traveling through a non-magnetic dielectric medium of relative permittivity $\epsilon_r$. If the amplitude of the electric field in the medium is $E_0$ and the speed of light in vacuum is $c$, the amplitude of the magnetic field $B_0$ in the medium is:
6a7a1ff8af9e6877547963da.sol:
The speed of an electromagnetic wave in a medium is given by:
$v = \dfrac{c}{\sqrt{\mu_r \epsilon_r}}$

For a non-magnetic medium, the relative permeability $\mu_r = 1$. Therefore, the speed of the wave in the dielectric medium is:
$v = \dfrac{c}{\sqrt{\epsilon_r}}$

The ratio of the electric field amplitude to the magnetic field amplitude in any medium is equal to the speed of the wave in that medium:
$\dfrac{E_0}{B_0} = v$

Substituting the expression for $v$, we get:
$\dfrac{E_0}{B_0} = \dfrac{c}{\sqrt{\epsilon_r}}$

Rearranging to solve for $B_0$, we obtain:
$B_0 = \dfrac{E_0 \sqrt{\epsilon_r}}{c}$

Answer: $B_0 = \dfrac{E_0 \sqrt{\epsilon_r}}{c}$

6a7a1ff8d3bfad6a5b8ad881.subject: Physics
6a7a1ff8d3bfad6a5b8ad881.text: A point object is placed on the principal axis of a convex lens of focal length $20 \text{ cm}$. A plane mirror is placed at a distance of $10 \text{ cm}$ behind the lens. The light rays from the object pass through the lens, get reflected by the plane mirror, and then pass through the lens again. If the final image is formed at a distance of $40 \text{ cm}$ in front of the lens, the distance of the original object from the lens is ____ $\text{cm}$.
6a7a1ff8d3bfad6a5b8ad881.sol:
Let us trace the image formation backwards. The final image is formed after the second refraction through the lens at a distance of $40 \text{ cm}$ in front of it. By sign convention, $v_2 = -40 \text{ cm}$.

Applying the lens formula for the second refraction:
$\dfrac{1}{v_2} - \dfrac{1}{u_2} = \dfrac{1}{f}$
$\dfrac{1}{-40} - \dfrac{1}{u_2} = \dfrac{1}{20}$
$\dfrac{1}{u_2} = -\dfrac{1}{40} - \dfrac{1}{20} = -\dfrac{3}{40}$
$u_2 = -\dfrac{40}{3} \text{ cm}$

This object for the second refraction is the image formed by the plane mirror, located $\dfrac{40}{3} \text{ cm}$ in front of the lens. Since the mirror is $10 \text{ cm}$ behind the lens, this image is at a distance of $10 + \dfrac{40}{3} = \dfrac{70}{3} \text{ cm}$ in front of the mirror.

For a plane mirror, the object distance equals the image distance. Thus, the object for the plane mirror (which is the image formed by the first refraction through the lens) must be $\dfrac{70}{3} \text{ cm}$ behind the mirror.

The distance of this first image from the lens is:
$v_1 = 10 + \dfrac{70}{3} = \dfrac{100}{3} \text{ cm}$

Applying the lens formula for the first refraction to find the original object distance $u_1$:
$\dfrac{1}{v_1} - \dfrac{1}{u_1} = \dfrac{1}{f}$
$\dfrac{3}{100} - \dfrac{1}{u_1} = \dfrac{1}{20}$
$\dfrac{1}{u_1} = \dfrac{3}{100} - \dfrac{1}{20} = \dfrac{3 - 5}{100} = -\dfrac{2}{100} = -\dfrac{1}{50}$
$u_1 = -50 \text{ cm}$

The distance of the original object from the lens is $50 \text{ cm}$.

Answer: $50$

6a7a1ff869d647711aec4031.subject: Physics
6a7a1ff869d647711aec4031.text:
In a logic circuit, inputs $A$ and $B$ are connected to the anodes of two ideal p-n junction diodes $D_1$ and $D_2$ respectively. The cathodes of both diodes are joined together at a node $X$, which is grounded through a resistor $R$. The voltage signal at node $X$ is fed to one input of a two-input NAND gate. A third input signal $C$ is fed to the other input of the NAND gate. The final output of the NAND gate is $Y$.

The logic levels for the inputs $A$, $B$, and $C$ over four consecutive time intervals are given as follows:
Interval 1: $A = 0$, $B = 0$, $C = 1$
Interval 2: $A = 0$, $B = 1$, $C = 1$
Interval 3: $A = 1$, $B = 0$, $C = 0$
Interval 4: $A = 1$, $B = 1$, $C = 1$

What is the sequence of logic levels for the output $Y$ in these four intervals?
6a7a1ff869d647711aec4031.sol:
The circuit consists of a diode-resistor logic gate followed by a NAND gate.

For the diode-resistor circuit: when either input $A$ or $B$ is at logic $1$ (high voltage), the corresponding diode is forward-biased, and the voltage at node $X$ becomes high (logic $1$). When both $A$ and $B$ are at logic $0$, both diodes are unbiased, and node $X$ is pulled to ground (logic $0$) through the resistor $R$.
Thus, the logic at node $X$ represents an OR gate: $X = A + B$.

The signal $X$ and input $C$ are fed into a NAND gate. The final output $Y$ is given by:
$Y = \overline{X \cdot C} = \overline{(A + B) \cdot C}$

Let us evaluate $Y$ for each time interval:
Interval 1: $A = 0$, $B = 0 \Rightarrow X = 0 + 0 = 0$. With $C = 1$, $Y = \overline{0 \cdot 1} = 1$.
Interval 2: $A = 0$, $B = 1 \Rightarrow X = 0 + 1 = 1$. With $C = 1$, $Y = \overline{1 \cdot 1} = 0$.
Interval 3: $A = 1$, $B = 0 \Rightarrow X = 1 + 0 = 1$. With $C = 0$, $Y = \overline{1 \cdot 0} = 1$.
Interval 4: $A = 1$, $B = 1 \Rightarrow X = 1 + 1 = 1$. With $C = 1$, $Y = \overline{1 \cdot 1} = 0$.

The sequence of logic levels for output $Y$ is $1, 0, 1, 0$.

Answer: $1, 0, 1, 0$

6a7a1ff8babc43c8f6cdc127.text: An aromatic compound $P$ having the molecular formula $C_6H_6O$ reacts with dilute $HNO_3$ to yield two isomers $A$ and $B$. Isomer $A$ is steam volatile due to intramolecular hydrogen bonding, whereas isomer $B$ is not steam volatile. Isomer $B$ is treated with aqueous $NaOH$ followed by the addition of ethyl bromide to yield compound $C$. The total number of hydrogen atoms present in one molecule of compound $C$ is
6a7a1ff8babc43c8f6cdc127.sol:
Compound $P$ ($C_6H_6O$) is phenol.

Nitration of phenol with dilute $HNO_3$ yields a mixture of ortho-nitrophenol and para-nitrophenol. Ortho-nitrophenol (isomer $A$) is steam volatile due to intramolecular hydrogen bonding, while para-nitrophenol (isomer $B$) is not steam volatile due to intermolecular hydrogen bonding.

When para-nitrophenol ($B$) is treated with aqueous $NaOH$, it forms sodium para-nitrophenoxide. This phenoxide ion undergoes Williamson ether synthesis upon reaction with ethyl bromide ($CH_3CH_2Br$) to yield para-nitrophenetole (1-ethoxy-4-nitrobenzene) as compound $C$.

The structure of compound $C$ is $C_6H_4(NO_2)(OCH_2CH_3)$.

Counting the hydrogen atoms: there are 4 hydrogen atoms on the benzene ring and 5 hydrogen atoms in the ethyl group.

Total number of hydrogen atoms = $4 + 5 = 9$.

Answer: $9$

6a7a1ff8409f8d1e9924095f.subject: Chemistry
6a7a1ff8409f8d1e9924095f.text:
In a chemical reaction, benzene is nitrated to produce nitrobenzene with a $60\%$ yield. The mass of benzene required to produce $12.3 \text{ g}$ of nitrobenzene is ________ $\text{g}$.

(Given atomic masses in $\text{g mol}^{-1}$: $\text{C}=12$, $\text{H}=1$, $\text{N}=14$, $\text{O}=16$)
6a7a1ff8409f8d1e9924095f.sol:
Molar mass of nitrobenzene ($\text{C}_6\text{H}_5\text{NO}_2$) $= (6 \times 12) + (5 \times 1) + 14 + (2 \times 16) = 123 \text{ g mol}^{-1}$

Moles of nitrobenzene produced $= \dfrac{12.3}{123} = 0.1 \text{ mol}$

Since the percentage yield is $60\%$, the theoretical moles of nitrobenzene required $= \dfrac{0.1}{0.6} = \dfrac{1}{6} \text{ mol}$

The nitration of benzene ($\text{C}_6\text{H}_6 \rightarrow \text{C}_6\text{H}_5\text{NO}_2$) has a $1:1$ stoichiometry, so the moles of benzene required $= \dfrac{1}{6} \text{ mol}$

Molar mass of benzene ($\text{C}_6\text{H}_6$) $= 78 \text{ g mol}^{-1}$

Mass of benzene required $= \dfrac{1}{6} \times 78 = 13 \text{ g}$

Answer: $13$

6a7a1ff8704a4564486398e0.text:
Consider the following statements:
(A) The dipole moment of $\text{NH}_3$ is greater than that of $\text{NF}_3$.
(B) Both $\text{O}_2$ and $\text{B}_2$ are paramagnetic molecules according to Molecular Orbital Theory.
(C) The shape of $\text{SF}_4$ is square planar.
(D) $\text{CO}$ and $\text{NO}^+$ are isoelectronic but have different bond orders.

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
6a7a1ff8704a4564486398e0.sol:
In $\text{NH}_3$, the orbital dipole due to the lone pair is in the same direction as the resultant dipole moment of the N-H bonds, whereas in $\text{NF}_3$, the orbital dipole is in the opposite direction to the resultant dipole moment of the N-F bonds. Thus, the dipole moment of $\text{NH}_3$ is greater than that of $\text{NF}_3$. Statement (A) is correct.

According to Molecular Orbital Theory, $\text{O}_2$ has two unpaired electrons in its $\pi^{*}$ antibonding orbitals, and $\text{B}_2$ has two unpaired electrons in its $\pi$ bonding orbitals. Both are paramagnetic. Statement (B) is correct.

In $\text{SF}_4$, sulfur has 4 bond pairs and 1 lone pair, resulting in a see-saw shape, not square planar. Statement (C) is incorrect.

$\text{CO}$ and $\text{NO}^+$ both have 14 electrons. They are isoelectronic and both have a bond order of 3. Statement (D) is incorrect.

Therefore, only statements (A) and (B) are correct.

Answer: (A) and (B) only
